thread.title: Hammett to seek emergency animal shelter assistance - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Hammett to seek emergency animal shelter assistance - NewsBreak

author: Isabella Kelly-Goss
title: Hammett to seek emergency animal shelter assistance - NewsBreak
text: Pasquotank Manager Sparty Hammett has been authorized to seek emergency assistance from neighboring county animal shelters and rescues, following Monday’s announcement that the local SPCA has been ordered to suspend shelter operations. The Pasquotank Board of Commissioners granted Hammett the authority on Monday. “While the lack of the shelter for our citizens is problematic enough, there are two other categories of dogs that the county will have to identify space to house,” Hammett said. The manager was referring to dogs designated by county animal services as dangerous and stray or roaming dogs. As part of a temporary solution, Hammett told the commissioners that he had begun speaking with Currituck and Chowan counties to try and put an emergency aid agreement in place. Hammett requested the board authorize him to move forward with his initial conversations with the counties. The commissioners voted 6-0 to grant Hammett’s request. Commissioner Sam Davis was not present to vote. On Monday, SPCA Board President Lillian Maland received a letter from the state’s Veterinary Division stating the SPCA’s shelter certificate is “suspended due to the shelter’s severe, repeated and willful violations” of the state’s Animal Welfare Act. “The SPCA staff and board are stunned and saddened by this news. All of us are here for one reason– to love and care for these precious animals,” Maland said in a statement to the public. “We are asking for your support and trust as we navigate the situation appropriately so we can continue to do this critical work.” The Veterinary Division is a service of the N.C. Department of Agriculture and Consumer Science. This notice of suspension came after the SPCA received a notice of fines totaling $14,750, on Aug. 1. The fines stem from more than 70 violations found by a state shelter inspector in late July. According to state documents, the violations include 30 counts of animals not having access to fresh water, 25 counts of animals not receiving proper rabies vaccinations, and multiple violations of incorrect record keeping. One term of the suspension requires that the SPCA rehouse all animals in its care within 30 days. The animals may not be adopted or fostered out, but must be placed in the care of another shelter or rescue that complies with AWA standards. The SPCA board held an emergency meeting Monday night to begin formulating a plan. For the duration of the suspension, the shelter is not allowed to take in additional animals, with the exception of animals brought in by Pasquotank Animal Services for a 10-day rabies observation period after the animal is believed to have bitten someone. According to the notice, the shelter could face legal consequences, including a fine of up to $5,000 per violation, if it continues to function as a shelter or perform shelter–related activities other than rabies observations. Pasquotank, as well as Camden counties, contract with the SPCA for animal services. In July, the Camden Commissioners chose to renew their SPCA contract for only 6 months, as opposed to the usual year-long agreement, in order to explore other shelter alternatives. Camden Manager Erin Burke recommended that they sign for 6 months while they began talks with neighboring shelters, such as Currituck’s. On Tuesday, Camden county officials issued a statement stating they, “share the community’s concern for the wellbeing of the animals involved” and believe the suspension to be “a necessary step to ensure compliance with animal welfare standards.” The SPCA has a 5-day grace period to file an appeal, though there has been no announcement to do so.
